flawed_step: Step 2: asserting that every degree-at-least-2 vertex in an arbitrary eligible tree has a leaf neighbor is unjustified; it already fails for the 5-vertex path.
counterexample: Let T be the path on V={1,2,3,4,5} with E={{1,2},{2,3},{3,4},{4,5}}. This is a tree with n=5, within 2<=n<=7. Its degrees are deg(1)=deg(5)=1 and deg(2)=deg(3)=deg(4)=2, so precisely vertices 1 and 5 are leaves. Vertex 3 has degree 2, but its neighbors are 2 and 4, both of degree 2; hence vertex 3 is adjacent to no leaf.
assessment_summary: The universal statement is false. A proof attempt may begin by choosing an arbitrary eligible tree, but the required property cannot then be established: the explicit path P5 supplies a checked counterexample.
